=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- File: tests/inventory_parity.py
  Line or code reference: lines 140-160 (parse_inventory) and lines 125-138 (load_exemptions)
  Problem: Inconsistent error handling between secondary document validation and inventory/exemptions parsing. While validate_secondary_documents() catches OSError and produces structured "FAIL:" messages, parse_inventory() and load_exemptions() raise SystemExit directly for malformed entries.
  Why it fails at runtime: Downstream consumers expecting structured failure output will receive a raw traceback instead of a "FAIL:" line when inventory.md or exemptions.txt have formatting errors, breaking error parsing contracts.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: tests/inventory_parity.py
  Line or code reference: lines 52-69 (EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE)
  Problem: The EXAMPLE_PREFIX_RE pattern uses an end-of-string anchor ($) that limits matches to prefixes appearing at the very end of a line, but the regex is applied via search() which looks anywhere in the line. This means patterns like "such as `scripts/foo.sh`" (with content after) will not be matched.
  Why it fails at runtime: Code span references following "such as" or "for example" on the same line will not be filtered out as examples, potentially causing false-positive "unexpected tracked-surface reference" failures if documentation includes example paths.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: tests/inventory_parity.py
  Line or code reference: lines 133-157 (parse_secondary_document)
  Problem: The function reads entire files into memory without size limits, which could cause memory issues with unexpectedly large files.
  Why it fails at runtime: If README.md or agents.md grow unexpectedly large (e.g., due to automated content injection), the read_text() call could consume excessive memory.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: tests/inventory_parity.py
  Line or code reference: validate_secondary_documents (lines 190-200)
  Problem: The try/except block catches OSError, but parse_secondary_document() calls document_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), which raises UnicodeDecodeError on files containing non-UTF-8 byte sequences. UnicodeDecodeError is a subclass of ValueError, not OSError, so it propagates uncaught and crashes the parity gate.
  Why it fails at runtime: If README.md or agents.md contains any non-UTF-8 content (e.g., a stray byte, copy-pasted smart quote converted to a lone byte, or a UTF-8 BOM not handled), the script terminates with an unhandled UnicodeDecodeError traceback rather than producing a structured FAIL: line.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
